title: South Shore Station, 114 East 11th Street, Michigan City, La Porte County, IN
notes: Significance: The South Shore Station (also called the 11th Street Station) is significant under Criterion A as the earliest, if not the only, purpose-built, multimodal transportation facility of the early twentieth century in La Porte County, Indiana. The South Shore Station was a central transportation hub, serving both rail and bus passengers, as well as freight lines. The Shore Line Motor Coach Company, which operated out of the Michigan City station, ran 26 bus routes in northern Indiana, southern Michigan, and Illinois. The station is furthermore representative of Samuel Insull's investment in and transformation of the Chicago South Shore & South Bend Railroad (CSS & SB), also known as the South Shore Line (SSL). The building is one of two extant early twentieth century stations of the SSL, both designed by Arthur Gerber. The South Shore Station is also significant under Criterion C as an example of Gerber's train stations in the greater Chicago area and is indicative of the Beaux Arts style that he characteristically employed in his designs for stations along the Chicago Rapid Transit Line. The South Shore Station is a contributing resource to the Franklin Street Commercial Historic District, listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) under Criteria A and C.
